name: Collecting duct: principal cell
summary: Where the final amounts are set by hormones. Aldosterone adds ENaC and Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase: Na⁺ reabsorbed, K⁺ secreted (through ROMK and BK). ADH inserts aquaporin-2 so water follows the medullary gradient, and opens urea channels in the inner medulla. Drugs: K⁺-sparing diuretics (amiloride, triamterene on ENaC; spironolactone, eplerenone on the receptor); vaptans block ADH’s V2 receptor.
tissue: kidney: collecting duct (cortex to inner medulla)

links.via: the other cell type lining the duct

na_l.name: Na⁺ (lumen)
na_l.notes: Only about 3% of filtered Na⁺ is left to reabsorb here, but this is where aldosterone sets the final amount.

k_l.name: K⁺ (lumen)
k_l.notes: Most of the K⁺ in urine was secreted here.

enac.name: ENaC (epithelial Na⁺ channel)
enac.notes: Apical Na⁺ channel. Aldosterone (through the mineralocorticoid receptor) adds ENaC and Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase; spironolactone and eplerenone block the receptor; amiloride and triamterene block ENaC (K⁺-sparing diuretics). Liddle syndrome: ENaC that is not removed (gain of function): hypertension, hypokalemia, low renin and aldosterone. The lumen-negative voltage it makes drives K⁺ and H⁺ secretion.

nak.name: Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase
nak.notes: On the basolateral side of every tubular cell: 3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in, using ATP. Keeping cell Na⁺ low is what drives every apical Na⁺ carrier (secondary active transport).

romk.name: ROMK and BK (K⁺ channels)
romk.notes: Secrete K⁺ into the lumen: more with aldosterone, with high flow and with more Na⁺ reaching here, which is why loop and thiazide diuretics cause hypokalemia (and K⁺-sparing diuretics do not).

aqp2.name: Aquaporin-2 (ADH)
aqp2.notes: ADH (vasopressin) binds V2 receptors → cAMP → AQP2 inserted in the apical membrane, and water follows the hypertonic medulla (concentrated urine). Central diabetes insipidus: no ADH (desmopressin works). Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus: V2 or AQP2 defects, lithium, demeclocycline. SIADH: too much ADH (vaptans block V2).

aqp34.name: Aquaporin-3 and aquaporin-4
aqp34.notes: Always-open basolateral water channels: water leaves the cell for the blood.

uta1.name: UT-A1 (urea channel, ADH)
uta1.notes: In the inner medullary collecting duct; ADH adds more. Urea leaves into the medulla, building its osmolality so more water can be pulled out.

uta3.name: UT-A3 (urea channel)
uta3.notes: Basolateral urea exit to the interstitium.

drugs.name: Amiloride
drugs.note: Blocks ENaC (triamterene too): a potassium-sparing diuretic; Liddle syndrome, lithium-induced nephrogenic DI.

diseases.name: Liddle syndrome
diseases.clue: Early hypertension, hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis with low renin and low aldosterone (ENaC stuck open); treat with amiloride.

drugs.name: Vaptans
drugs.note: Block the V2 receptor, so no aquaporin-2 in the membrane: SIADH, hyponatremia (tolvaptan, conivaptan).

drugs.name: Lithium
drugs.note: Blunts ADH’s effect on aquaporin-2 insertion: nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (demeclocycline likewise).

diseases.name: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
diseases.clue: Large volumes of dilute urine that desmopressin does not concentrate (V2 receptor or aquaporin-2 defect; lithium).
